reason: Section 2 establishes the Committee for the Preservation of the White House (members: the Director of the National Park Service as Chairman, the Curator, the Secretary of the Smithsonian Institution, the Chairman of the Commission of Fine Arts, the Director of the National Gallery of Art, the Chief Usher, and seven other members appointed by the President; members serve without compensation). Executive Order 11565 (October 13, 1970, effective on signing) substituted a new section 2 that is the same except that the seven other members became so many other members as the President may from time to time appoint (before: seven appointed members; after: such number as the President appoints). The substance of the membership rule changed in that respect only. Each biennial continuation order since 1975, listed as a later event with its signing date, continued the Committee without changing this provision; the latest, Executive Order 14354 (2025), continues it until September 30, 2027. The Committee is therefore in existence on 2026-10-14 and the clause is operative.

Section 1-102 says that until the Office of Personnel Management is established (on or before January 1, 1979), pursuant to Reorganization Plan No. 2 of 1978, the Civil Service Commission shall exercise the authority delegated under the order. The condition occurred on January 1, 1979: the held text of Executive Order 12107, section 1-101, makes the establishment of the Office of Personnel Management under the Reorganization Plan effective on that date, and section 1-102's own wording sets that date as the latest. The actor is the order itself (own terms); the first end is the date the Office of Personnel Management was established, January 1, 1979, so the Civil Service Commission's exercise ended then. The inclusive reading (the clause runs through the end of December 31, 1978) and the alternative reading (the clause ends when January 1, 1979 begins) coincide in practice because the condition is the establishment of a body on that day.
